title: Mediated Studies In Respiratory Therapy Iv
description: Fourth of seven courses paralleling content taught in courses in the Respiratory Therapy Program. Designed to develop and reinforce concepts taught in the concurrent lecture and laboratory sessions of the program, with a focus on modes of ventilation, waveform recognition, clinical application, lung recruitment techniques, and adjunct therapies for ventilated patients. Media materials, simulations, and videos will provide alternative learning resources to accommodate diverse learning styles. Intended for students in the Respiratory Therapy Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Distinguishes between the different modes of ventilation.
objectives: Differentiate between the different modes of ventilation.
Recognize auto-peep and demonstrate strategies to correct it.
Describe and recognize alveolar micro-strain and stress.
Explain indications and use of inhaled nitric oxide.
Describe the use and application of the Passy Muir Valve.
content: APRV as a lung recruitment strategy
Strategies to avoid micro-strain and stress
Available sources for the delivery of INO
PMV for early intervention for the ICU patient
